contrary_evidence: Carnegie research on wartime Ukraine finds visible military impact of cyber operations less decisive than many predictions, despite technically significant intrusions and civilian losses.
Real AI-enabled intrusions and agent errors do not demonstrate universal autonomous geopolitical campaign capabilities; platform-specific observational samples cannot estimate global prevalence.
Recovery, offline controls and trusted partnerships can limit civilian and physical impact even where advanced malware has reached operational environments.
limitations: Historical state attribution varies by source and standard of proof; official charges are presented as official allegations, not definitive proof for every incident.
Anthropic's 832-account sample is selected from one provider; changes in internal risk classifications are not global cybercrime statistics.
Long-run cyber and AI scenarios are conditional, lack empirically defensible exact probabilities and must not be read as technology timelines.
The literature and incident record are unevenly observable because many intelligence operations remain classified and successful defense may not generate public evidence.

contrary_evidence: February 2026 Estonian foreign intelligence assessed no Russian intention to attack NATO within the following year.
September 2026 Danish intelligence described a broad conventional invasion as highly unlikely and no visible preparation, while noting low but rising risk of limited military attack.
NATO's defence commitments and nuclear deterrence can reduce incentives for deliberate major war even while proximity and incidents create risk.
limitations: A hypothetical war has no empirically justifiable start date, duration, nuclear escalation probability or global casualty count.
Intelligence judgments reflect limited horizons, assumptions and possible unknown decision-making; they are not direct measurements of all state intentions.
SIPRI military spending, nuclear inventories and capacity figures are estimates; monetary totals do not measure theatre-specific operational readiness.
Scenario horizons are conceptual and not likelihood weights; economic and psychological consequences require country- and group-specific exposure data.
Historical background and contemporary incident attribution are distinct evidentiary tasks; no claimed anonymous sabotage is treated as verified.

title: AI is making software and cognitive work more abundant — while concentrating the infrastructure that produces them
deck: Falling task and application costs are compressing entry-level work and generic software rents while compute, energy, data, distribution and trusted workflows become scarcer and more strategic.
regime: AI is lowering the cost of digital production faster than the physical and institutional inputs required to deploy it at scale.
key_risk: Productivity gains may coexist with weaker entry-level career ladders and a larger share of economic rents accruing to infrastructure, distribution and capital owners.

signal_rationale.delta: By October 2026, evidence from labour markets, software valuations, pricing models, cloud regulation and energy infrastructure can be connected into one observable shift: AI is reducing the scarcity of some cognitive tasks and application features while raising the strategic scarcity of compute, power, capital, distribution and trusted workflows.
signal_rationale.evidence: The assessment triangulates Stanford labour and investment data, ILO and OECD occupational exposure, NBER and METR productivity evidence, SEG and Stripe software-market data, Salesforce pricing, IEA physical-infrastructure data, FTC and European Commission competition work, Microsoft filings and clearly labelled investor theses.
signal_rationale.scale_path: Further diffusion depends on lower model and inference costs, reliable agentic workflows and organizational redesign; concentration depends on whether chips, electricity, grid access, cloud, proprietary data and distribution remain scale-constrained.
signal_rationale.transmission: The shift transmits through entry-level hiring, apprenticeship structures, software pricing and valuation, capital allocation, electricity systems, cloud dependence, bargaining power and international distribution of technology rents.
signal_rationale.falsifier: The thesis weakens if exposed young-worker hiring recovers while AI adoption rises, seat-based software pricing remains dominant in agentic workflows, generic application margins retain durable premiums, and cloud/compute/energy bottlenecks and concentration fall materially.

selection_rationale: The canonical Europe–Russia–Ukraine security-system report explicitly distinguishes Poland and the Baltic states because historical memory and geographic proximity make Russian military power a more immediate national-security variable. contrary_evidence: Defence spending above 5% of GDP and proximity to Russia support a high-security-burden thesis, while euro-area membership, moderate debt, strong institutions and sustained growth argue against treating Lithuania as economically fragile.
Population decline and ageing constrain labour supply, but positive international migration and high wage growth have recently supported employment and domestic demand.

Russian electricity-system dependence has ended and LNG plus renewables have diversified supply, but imports, interconnections and storage remain necessary, so energy independence should not be described as autarky.
A small domestic market constrains scale, while lasers, fintech and higher-technology manufacturing demonstrate that deep EU integration and specialised exports can overcome some scale limits.
limitations: 2026 growth and inflation forecasts vary by source and forecast date; they are attributed rather than averaged.

Renewable shares of domestic generation and of total electricity demand are different measures and are kept separate.

RRF payment requests and milestone completion do not directly measure long-run productivity outcomes.
Security framing in official Lithuanian sources reflects the state's documented policy assessment; factual capabilities and expenditures are separated from political interpretation.

selection_rationale: Portugal is an EU, euro-area and NATO member whose fiscal repair, Atlantic geography, renewable-heavy power system, tourism-dependent external balance and migration-supported labour supply create mechanisms not covered by existing France, Germany or European security dossiers. A reusable Portuguese country context is needed to analyse Iberian energy integration, Atlantic logistics and defence, southern-European productivity convergence and the post-RRF investment transition without reconstructing the same structural background.
contrary_evidence: Sharp public-debt reduction, repeated fiscal surpluses, historically low unemployment and stronger bank balance sheets support a resilience thesis, while debt remains high, ageing pressures are rising and productivity convergence remains weak.

Immigration has reversed population decline and expanded labour supply, while a very high ageing index and slower migration in 2025 show that demographic constraints have been mitigated rather than solved.

Renewables already supply most electricity consumption and can support industrial investment, while imported fuels, system-integration needs and the Iberian blackout demonstrate that electricity abundance is not equivalent to complete energy autonomy.

Housing price increases are extreme, but limited mortgage-credit expansion and stronger banks indicate that structural supply restrictions are currently a clearer mechanism than a repeat of the pre-2011 credit cycle.
limitations: Portugal revised its 2021–2025 population series using a new administrative-data methodology, so demographic comparisons must use consistent vintages.
Second-quarter 2026 GDP was revised after the flash estimate; observed quarterly data and annual forecasts are kept separate.
PRR milestone completion and payment requests do not directly measure completed productive capital or long-run productivity effects.
Housing transaction prices and new-contract rents do not by themselves measure affordability.
Renewable electricity shares cannot be extrapolated to total final energy consumption.
The ENTSO-E blackout report describes a multi-factor interconnected-system event and should not be reduced to a single-country or single-technology cause.
The NATO 2% accounting measure does not directly measure operational readiness or domestic defence-industry output.

Revision 1 corrects the Q2 2026 year-on-year GDP figure to the current INE value of 2.5% and adds the required evidence-bearing geographic map in both locales; the broader analytical thesis is unchanged.

selection_rationale: The public corpus contains a focused study of Israel's 1985 stabilization but lacks a reusable country-level dossier linking state formation, constitutional institutions, security mobilisation, high technology, defence industry, fiscal capacity, demographics, energy and water systems, regional normalisation, and the economic mechanisms connecting Israel with the West Bank and Gaza. Israel is also directly connected to existing Iran, Saudi Arabia and United States country research, making a structural dossier necessary to avoid repeatedly rebuilding context in regional research.
contrary_evidence: Large foreign-exchange reserves, a resilient financial system, strong high-tech exports and repeated post-shock recoveries argue against a simple thesis of economic fragility.
Rising debt, repeated reserve mobilisation, infrastructure gaps and relocation of some R&D activity abroad argue against treating wartime resilience as costless or indefinitely self-renewing.

Peace treaties and regional normalisation demonstrate substantial interstate integration, while the unresolved Israeli-Palestinian conflict and continuing regional military confrontation limit any claim that geopolitical risk has structurally disappeared.
A young population can enlarge future labour supply, but uneven employment and skill formation across rapidly growing groups mean demographic growth is not automatically a fiscal dividend.
limitations: Israeli and Palestinian statistical systems use different territorial coverage; population and GDP series must not be combined without explicit scope reconciliation.
Wartime fiscal and defence figures use different accounting perimeters and are frequently revised as operations and reserves change.
Active-conflict casualty, damage and displacement figures can be incomplete or differently defined across Israeli, Palestinian and UN sources.
The ICJ source is an advisory opinion with separate and dissenting opinions; its legal conclusions are attributed precisely and not treated as a negotiated political settlement.
Current macroeconomic forecasts are highly conditional on security assumptions and differ between the IMF and Bank of Israel.
The 27 October 2026 election had not occurred by the evidence cutoff, so no electoral outcome is inferred.

selection_rationale: Ukraine is a central actor in the existing Europe–Russia–Ukraine conflict-system report, but the public corpus lacked a reusable country-level dossier on how the Ukrainian state, war economy, reconstruction requirement, external financing, EU accession, defence industry, demographics, energy system and regional economic geography interact. The dossier avoids duplicating the conflict-history report and instead focuses on the internal political economy and reconstruction mechanisms required by current and future research.
contrary_evidence: Ukraine's massive physical damage, demographic displacement and dependence on official finance argue against treating wartime institutional continuity as evidence of normal economic conditions.
Functioning banks, continued exports, domestic defence production, digital administration and progress toward EU accession argue against a state-collapse narrative.

Large reconstruction needs create investment opportunity but do not guarantee growth because security risk, governance, labour supply, insurance and project execution determine whether capital becomes productive capacity.
limitations: Population, labour-force and migration denominators are unusually uncertain under occupation, displacement and wartime administrative conditions.

IMF and NBU forecasts remain highly conditional on security assumptions and external-financing continuity.

selection_rationale: Published canonical research already treats Temasek and Singapore's sovereign-capital architecture as a material transmission mechanism, but the corpus lacks country-level context connecting reserves, CPF, public housing, land, monetary policy, logistics, finance, industrial upgrading, foreign labour, demography and external strategy. This dossier supplies that reusable structural context without duplicating the existing actor studies.
contrary_evidence: Singapore's high gross public-debt ratio is not evidence of conventional fiscal distress because the Government reports a positive net asset position and most borrowing proceeds cannot finance recurrent spending; gross liabilities still require prudent management.
Public housing supports unusually broad owner-occupation, while 99-year lease decay, affordability and CPF withdrawals create genuine intergenerational and retirement trade-offs.
Foreign labour materially expands productive capacity, but it also creates a segmented labour market and additional housing, transport and social-integration pressures.

Singapore's port, financial and legal ecosystems are dense and difficult to reproduce quickly, while neighbouring economies continue improving infrastructure, talent and direct-connectivity alternatives.

Semiconductor investment is structurally important, but Singapore does not control the global leading-edge logic foundry chokepoint and remains heavily dependent on multinational firms and imported technology.

Deep security ties with the United States and deep economic relations with China coexist; the evidence supports issue-specific diversification rather than simple geopolitical equidistance or exclusive alignment.
limitations: The total value of Singapore's national reserves is not publicly disclosed, and GIC does not disclose assets under management; third-party AUM estimates should not be treated as official figures.
Temasek's publicly reported net portfolio value is not equivalent to the stock of national reserves.
EDB fixed-asset-investment commitments are expected projects and should not be treated as already-realised investment.
The 6 GW low-carbon electricity-import target is planned capacity for 2035, not operating supply today.
Population statistics distinguish citizens, permanent residents and non-residents; total population alone obscures labour-market, infrastructure and political implications.

Political and civil-liberties assessments use source classes with different functions: official sources establish laws and institutional design, while external rights organisations provide attributed criticism and case-based evidence.

key_constraints: Hong Kong's financial connector role increasingly depends on Mainland issuers and investors while international participation remains necessary for its offshore function
The Linked Exchange Rate System imports U.S. dollar monetary conditions and limits independent countercyclical interest-rate policy
Commercial real estate remains a material financial-sector risk even as residential property has broadly stabilised
Land-premium revenue has weakened while Northern Metropolis and other infrastructure require large capital expenditure and greater bond issuance
Rapid ageing and low natural population growth reduce labour-force participation, increasing reliance on talent and labour inflows
The Northern Metropolis must compete with nearby Shenzhen on industrial costs while relying on Hong Kong's finance, universities and institutional differentiation
Geopolitical and legal divergence between China and Western jurisdictions raises compliance costs for global firms using Hong Kong as an interface
selection_rationale: Hong Kong is undergoing a structural transition in which deeper integration with Mainland China's capital markets, technology system and spatial planning is occurring alongside continued operation of a separate currency, open capital account, tax system, customs territory and common-law commercial architecture. Strong 2025-26 capital-market recovery, a new infrastructure-and-technology planning cycle, demographic migration offsets and post-2020 institutional changes interact across economy, politics and society, making the case materially consequential and not reducible to a conventional country profile.
contrary_evidence: Strong IPO fundraising and turnover in 2025-26 contradict a simple claim that post-2020 political and legal changes mechanically caused financial collapse; they do not demonstrate that institutional change has zero economic cost.

Mainland integration expands issuer and investor flows through Stock Connect, Bond Connect and other schemes, while simultaneously increasing concentration in Mainland corporate activity and exposure to Mainland-specific risks.
The HKD peg imports U.S. monetary conditions and constrains domestic rate policy, but it also provides a credible currency anchor that remains central to international financial intermediation.

Residential property has broadly stabilised, while office and retail commercial property continue to face structural vacancy and refinancing pressure; 'the property market' cannot be treated as one cycle.
Population has returned to modest growth because of net inflows, but deaths exceed births and ageing continues to depress labour-force participation.
The Northern Metropolis creates large new technology and industrial capacity on paper, but private firm location, production scale and commercialisation outcomes remain unproven.
limitations: Hong Kong is a Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China rather than a sovereign state; the ISO code HK is used only for territorial indexing in the research taxonomy.
Official HKSAR and PRC sources establish laws, institutional design and stated policy rationales but are not independent measures of political rights or social effects.
External rights organisations provide documented cases and attributed critical interpretations but do not independently measure the full economic impact of national-security legislation.
Market activity cannot be used as a proxy for institutional legitimacy, and political criticism cannot be used as a proxy for financial decline.
Visa approvals do not equal resident retention or employment, and Northern Metropolis plans do not equal operating industrial capacity.
The IMF's May 2026 growth forecast predates stronger official second-quarter data; the report keeps the forecast and subsequent observations temporally distinct.

key_constraints: Leading-edge semiconductor capacity is geographically concentrated while relying on global equipment, materials, customers and logistics
Taiwan imports most primary energy and relies heavily on seaborne LNG and coal, making electricity resilience dependent on maritime access, storage and grid redundancy
Rapid aging and very low fertility constrain engineering, healthcare, construction and defense manpower simultaneously
AI and semiconductor demand currently dominate export and investment growth, increasing exposure to a concentrated technology cycle

Divided government and constitutional disputes can delay budget execution, energy policy, industrial measures and defense procurement
Water availability, grid quality, land and climate hazards constrain further concentration of advanced manufacturing in the western industrial corridor
selection_rationale: Taiwan is undergoing a consequential structural transition in which an AI-driven export boom, further concentration of leading-edge semiconductor production, a sharp reorientation of export demand toward the United States, demographic contraction, energy-security constraints and persistent cross-Strait military pressure are increasingly interacting. The case links economy, politics and society through observable production, infrastructure, institutional and security mechanisms and has direct transmission to global technology, trade and capital allocation.
contrary_evidence: The U.S. overtook mainland China and Hong Kong combined as Taiwan's largest export destination in 2025, but cross-Strait trade, investment and production networks remain large; the evidence supports rebalancing rather than decoupling.

TSMC is expanding capacity in the United States, Japan and Germany, but it is simultaneously adding leading-edge 2nm and advanced-packaging capacity in Taiwan; overseas diversification does not yet demonstrate domestic hollowing-out.

Taiwan's large current-account surplus and foreign-exchange reserves provide financial resilience but cannot substitute for imported energy, shipping access, water, electricity or critical production inputs during a physical disruption.

Competitive elections, alternation in power and constitutional review support institutional resilience, while divided government and budget disputes show that democratic checks can also slow policy execution.
Semiconductor concentration creates strong global incentives to avoid disruption, but there is no empirical basis for treating the so-called silicon shield as an automatic military deterrent.

Higher defense spending, longer conscription and civil-resilience planning increase capacity, while demographic decline, procurement delays and infrastructure dependencies limit the inference that spending alone determines readiness.
limitations: The legal and diplomatic status of Taiwan is contested. The research separates effective administration, constitutional claims, diplomatic recognition and institutional participation rather than adopting one actor's sovereignty formulation as fact.

PRC, Taiwan, U.S. and other official security statements are strategic communications as well as policy evidence; intentions are not inferred mechanically from military-activity counts or official rhetoric.
Semiconductor capacity and trade concentration are observable, but their effect on deterrence and crisis decisions is inferential.
Long-run demographic figures are conditional projections based on fertility, mortality and migration assumptions, not deterministic forecasts.
Military readiness, ammunition stocks, classified intelligence and crisis plans cannot be independently measured from public data with the same precision as macroeconomic or trade variables.
Exceptional 2025-2026 GDP and export growth reflects a concentrated AI and semiconductor cycle and should not be extrapolated mechanically as Taiwan's long-run trend growth.

en.key_risk: Taiwan's financial buffers and semiconductor leadership cannot by themselves offset a physical disruption to maritime energy, logistics, electricity, water or critical imported inputs; resilience depends on infrastructure, institutional execution and supply-chain redundancy as much as foreign-exchange capacity.

signal_rationale.delta: 2026 evidence shows enterprise agent usage moving from assistance toward delegated execution while new benchmarks and clinical research expose context integrity, multi-task reliability and selective-autonomy constraints that are not visible in simple model benchmarks.
signal_rationale.evidence: The signal triangulates provider telemetry, Microsoft Research enterprise benchmarks, a peer-reviewed Nature Medicine on-premise clinical-agent study and NIST's current TEVV work.
signal_rationale.scale_path: Scaling requires not only stronger models but identity, permissions, context segmentation, continuous evaluation, workflow-specific reliability gates, auditability and economical human escalation.
signal_rationale.transmission: Agents that can act across tools can change task composition, coordination cost, organizational design and demand for assurance infrastructure, while also creating privacy, accountability and distributional risks.
signal_rationale.falsifier: The thesis weakens if rising agent usage fails to translate into verified workflow performance, if supervision requirements scale nearly one-for-one with agent activity, or if contextual-integrity and multi-task reliability do not improve under realistic deployment.

signal_rationale.delta: CAPSTONE completed its extended demonstration phase in 2026 while NASA advanced a two-spacecraft follow-on, delivered navigation hardware for a commercial lunar relay, specified an initial five-satellite relay architecture and opened new lunar infrastructure procurement.
signal_rationale.evidence: The signal combines completed flight demonstration, flight-hardware delivery, contracted follow-on demonstration, service architecture, interoperability standards and current procurement rather than relying on a roadmap alone.
signal_rationale.scale_path: The path runs from autonomous navigation and relays to interoperable multi-provider services, then to persistent surface power, logistics, manufacturing and recurring multi-mission demand.

signal_rationale.falsifier: Repeated relay delays, failure of multi-provider interoperability, weak non-anchor demand or persistent surface-power/logistics bottlenecks that prevent growth of the lunar installed base would weaken the service-infrastructure thesis.

contrary_evidence: Dhra granaries precede the archaeological evidence of fully domesticated cereals, so storage, sedentism and domestication cannot be assumed synchronous.

The Kuk Swamp record shows early exploitation, later mounds and much later ditches rather than a single invention moment.
Huxi early rice spikelet bases contain 61.2% wild shattering, 30.1% intermediate and 8.7% domesticated-type bases, undermining instant completed domestication.
Present-day inferred origins and prehistoric archaeological first occurrences have heterogeneous dates, contexts and biological criteria.
limitations: Dates are site-specific and often calibrated BP; model-estimated pearl-millet expansion is not commensurable with an archaeological first appearance.
The cross-regional chronological chart compares selected indicative markers, not comparable dates of full domestication or quantitative productivity.

Skeletal proxies of health and workload capture selected people and cannot establish universal wellbeing changes.
DNA ancestry and domestication traits cannot by themselves identify ownership, legal entitlements or political coercion.
Review uses published source materials and secondary institutional summaries; it is not an independent peer-reviewed archaeological monograph.

contrary_evidence: Çatalhöyük 2024 20-building sample finds no enduring institutionalized wealth hierarchy but does identify temporary inequality and differentiated access to non-staple goods.

131 sampled ancient genomes in the 2025 Science study demonstrate maternal-line connections and changing burial-house kinship; they do not directly prove a female government, legal inheritance rules or universally sex-biased community migration.
2019 PNAS cranial injury observations (25 of 93, 12 with repeat injuries) identify interpersonal harm but do not identify state police, a professional army or the motives for each injury.
Subperiosteal skeletal reactions decrease 33%, 26%, 19% across Early/Middle/Late samples despite maximal crowding in Middle phase; density cannot be the sole infection mechanism.
Eastern Anatolian obsidian came from sources over 600 km away; geology does not reveal whether exchange used marriage, gifts, merchant intermediaries or direct travel.
UNESCO heritage East Mound occupation 7400–6200 BCE differs from detailed analytical period convention 7100–5950 cal BCE; different models and strata should remain explicit.
limitations: The UNESCO 37-hectare property includes both mounds and cannot be interpreted as the simultaneously occupied settlement area or a population census.

Two health charts show different osteological indicators and denominators; values must not be pooled into a sitewide disease incidence rate.
Cranial injuries with recurrent trauma are a subset of the 25 injured individuals among 93 analyzed; the chart bars cannot be added.
Gini-style archaeological household proxies from 20 comparatively excavated buildings are not observed currency income distributions.
Ancient genetic kinship captures biological relations among sampled buried people, not adoption legal status, religious offices or political leadership.
Obsidian-source provenance is not direct evidence of a trade contract, merchant expedition or market price.
Source verification is based on directly accessible academic sources and cited summaries, not external scholarly peer review.

selection_rationale: Full original longitudinal investigation of Argentine fiscal, monetary, external and social inflation mechanisms from national monetary formation and the 1890 banking collapse, through 1975, 1989–90, 1991–2001, 2018 and the observed 2024–September 2026 period, distinguished from existing concise country overview and 1991 policy case.
contrary_evidence: Nineteenth-century banking and exchange crises do not establish uninterrupted high CPI inflation since independence; chronic inflation primarily consolidated after 1945.
The 1991 peg genuinely achieved rapid disinflation before later collapse under external and debt constraints.
The 2018 sudden stop and 2001 crisis demonstrate debt and currency vulnerabilities not captured by money growth alone.
The inflation slowdown observed in 2024–2025 does not by itself resolve the reserves, growth, debt and income-distribution constraints.
2007–15 CPI/GDP reliability and methodological breaks limit long-run series comparability.
limitations: Historic monetary regimes and selected postwar inflation observations cannot be joined to modern nationally representative CPI as a homogeneous series.
Observed year-end 2023–2025 annual inflation, September 2026 monthly CPI and May 2026 IMF forecasts have distinct time frequencies and evidentiary status.
INDEC poverty refers to 31 urban agglomerations and half-year comparisons require seasonal and methodological care.
Fiscal, monetary, currency, wage indexation and external effects are not attributed an unsupported constant quantitative weight across different historical regimes.
Bibliography includes repeated foundational publications to align explanatory source use; distinct source counts must use unique works and hosts.

selection_rationale: The 2027 policy and investment horizon joins a 2026 high-rate monetary cycle, legislated CBS rollout, draft 2027 budget, provisionally applicable EU–Mercosur trade terms, new US trade barriers, Chinese commodity demand and persistent structural productivity constraints.
contrary_evidence: Forecasts range from 1.2% to 2.3% real GDP growth using different institutions, dates and model assumptions; none is a realised 2027 figure.
The 2027 draft budget's R$83.4 billion adjusted primary surplus differs from its R$18.6 billion full primary balance and should not be treated as the same fiscal outcome.
The EU–Mercosur interim trade agreement has been provisionally applied to Brazil since 1 May 2026, but measured investment and export effects require subsequent evidence.
China's large bilateral trade surplus does not identify Brazilian industrial competitiveness or future commodity prices.
BRICS payment interoperability and local-currency settlement are not a common currency or a unified capital market.
limitations: The 2027 budget remains a proposal as of the information cutoff; neither appropriation nor project pipeline constitutes executed spending.
2026 data from GDP, credit, fiscal and trade statistics have different observation dates and should not be presented as one synchronized monthly release.
GDP forecast vintages are shown for comparison, not as a statistical confidence interval or political performance ranking.
Underlying financial and market figures are from public institutional reporting and do not include firm-by-firm audited financial statements.
Conditional scenarios are not assigned subjective probabilities or invented GDP levels.

contrary_evidence: An economy can achieve productivity and consumer welfare gains while importing advanced intermediate goods; import dependence is not automatically evidence of industrial failure.

limitations: This is a structural multiregional report, not transaction-level tracking or a claim to enumerate all trade flows and routes.

The most recent cited official source vintages differ: 2024 maritime ton-miles and food trade, 2025 port cargo, 2026 Q2 energy chokepoints, and 2022 TiVA value-added estimates. They are never combined into a fictitious common-year ledger.
EIA chokepoint estimates rely partly on shipping tracking, not customs declarations; charted oil flows are quarterly averages, not full-year consumption.
Quantitative diagrams present sources and measurement limits; the regional map is analytical and does not imply vessel GPS tracks or precise coordinates.
